function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
The debate over who is the greatest basketball player ever is one of the most passionate and enduring discussions in sports history. While opinions vary—some point to LeBron James, others to Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar, and still others to Bill Russell—the consensus among many analysts, former players, and fans leans toward **Michael Jordan**.

### Why Michael Jordan?

| Category | Jordan’s Achievements |
|----------|-----------------------|
| **Championships** | 6 NBA titles (1991–1993, 1996–1998) |
| **MVP Awards** | 5 regular‑season MVPs (1988, 1991, 1992, 1996, 1998) |
| **Scoring Titles** | 10 scoring titles (1987–1993, 1996–1998) |
| **Defensive Impact** | 9 All‑Defensive First Team selections (1988–1993, 1996–1998) |
| **Clutch Performance** | 6 Finals MVPs, 6 NBA Finals appearances, 6 NBA Finals series wins |
| **Cultural Influence** | Global icon; helped popularize the NBA worldwide; iconic brand (Air Jordan) |
| **Statistical Legacy** | Career averages: 30.12 points, 6.22 rebounds, 5.30 assists per game |

### Key Points

1. **Dominance Across Eras** – Jordan’s performance was dominant even when the league had different rules, styles, and competition levels. He consistently outperformed his peers in both offensive and defensive categories.

2. **Consistency & Clutch** – Jordan’s ability to elevate his game in high‑pressure situations is legendary. His six Finals MVP awards underscore his impact when it mattered most.

3. **Influence Beyond the Court** – Jordan’s marketability and global reach transformed the NBA into a worldwide brand. His partnership with Nike created the Air Jordan line, which remains a cultural phenomenon.

4. **Comparisons to Other Greats** – While LeBron James has impressive longevity and versatility, Jordan’s combination of scoring prowess, defensive excellence, and championship success gives him a slight edge in many statistical comparisons. Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar’s scoring record is unmatched, but Jordan’s overall impact on the game’s popularity and style of play is often considered more transformative.

### Bottom Line

While the “greatest” title can be debated, Michael Jordan’s blend of individual brilliance, team success, and cultural influence places him at the top of most lists. That said, the conversation is always evolving, especially as current stars like LeBron James continue to add to their legacies.
